chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, who said:

I heard Abu Hamza saying, 'I heard Al-Abd Al-Salih (peace be upon him) saying: Whoever visits his believing brother for the sake of Allah, not for anything else, seeking by it the reward of Allah and the fulfillment of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has promised, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will assign to him seventy thousand angels from the time he leaves his house until he returns to it, calling out to him: "Indeed, you have done well, and Paradise is made better for you; you have taken a dwelling in Paradise."'

key_terms.أَلَا طِبْتَ: Indeed, you have done well / Be pleased
key_terms.الْعَبْدَ الصَّالِحَ: The Pious Servant (a title for Imam Musa al-Kazim, peace be upon him)
key_terms.لِلَّهِ: For the sake of Allah (indicating sincerity of intention)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting a believer with sincere intention?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, linking the act of Ziyarat to the Imamah tradition of the 'Abd al-Salih (often identified as Imam al-Sadiq or a specific title for the Imams). The promise of seventy thousand angels underscores the immense spiritual weight of maintaining social bonds among believers, a core tenet of Shia communal ethics. This reward is not merely for the visit itself but for the purity of intention (ikhlas), ensuring the act is solely for Allah's pleasure rather than social reciprocity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub who said, ‘I heard Abu Hamza saying,

‘I heard Al-Abd Al-Salihasws (7th Imamasws) saying: ‘The one who visits his brother Momin for the Sake of Allahazwj, not for anything else, seeking by it the Rewards of Allahazwj, and accomplishment of what Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Promised, Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic would Allocate seventy thousand Angels with him, from when he goes out from his house until he returns to it, calling out to him: ‘Indeed! You have done well, and the Paradise is (Made to be) better for you for assuming a house in the Paradise’’.
en.sarwar: 15. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Ayyub who has said the following: “

I heard abu Hamza saying, T heard the good servant (of Allah) saying, “Whoever visits his believing brother (in belief) for the sake of Allah and for no other reason, seeking thereby the reward from Allah, the promise of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will come true and Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will appoint seventy thousand angels, from the time he leaves his home to the time he returns home, applaud behind him, ‘How beautiful is your deed! How beautiful is paradise for you! You have found a dwelling in paradise.’”
